data.narrative:
HEO is a Series A stage company in Space & Aerospace founded by Dr. Will Crowe and Dr. Hiranya Jayakody. The target universe comprises 6 public Space & Aerospace peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs, though narrow same-stage comparables remain sparse in this sector.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable valuation approach, using HEO's $12M total raised as a base proxy and applying a 2.0x multiplier typical for Series A to subsequent stage transitions, yielding an implied valuation of $24M. Peer-median triangulation was not feasible due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the defined peer set; the broader Space & Aerospace cohort contained only 2 adjacent-stage datapoints, below the 3-point threshold for statistical reliability. Public-comp anchoring using the sector's median P/S multiple of 23.9x could not be applied because HEO's revenue is not disclosed—a common constraint for private companies.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $20M to $28M, with a median point of $24M. This range reflects limited triangulation depth: reliance on a single methodology introduces meaningful uncertainty around capital efficiency, burn profile, and technology differentiation relative to both public and private peers. Revenue disclosure or additional comparable transactions in early-stage space technology would strengthen conviction.
